section.heading: Find the Least Common Denominator of Rational Expressions
section.paragraph: When we add or subtract rational expressions with unlike denominators we will need to get common denominators. If we review the procedure we used with numerical fractions, we will know what to do with rational expressions.

Let’s look at the example $$\frac{7}{12} + \frac{5}{18}$$ from Foundations. Since the denominators are not the same, the first step was to find the least common denominator (LCD). Remember, the LCD is the least common multiple of the denominators. It is the smallest number we can use as a common denominator.

To find the LCD of 12 and 18, we factored each number into primes, lining up any common primes in columns. Then we “brought down” one prime from each column. Finally, we multiplied the factors to find the LCD.
We do the same thing for rational expressions. However, we leave the LCD in factored form.

note.paragraph: Remember, we always exclude values that would make the denominator zero. What values of x should we exclude in this next example?

section.heading: Find Equivalent Rational Expressions
section.paragraph: When we add numerical fractions, once we find the LCD, we rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction with the LCD.
We will do the same thing for rational expressions.

problem.paragraph: Rewrite as equivalent rational expressions with denominator $$(x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3)$$ : $$\frac{8}{x^{2} - 2x - 3},\frac{3x}{x^{2} + 4x + 3}.$$

row.cell: Multiply each denominator by the 'missing' factor and multiply each numerator by the same factor.

note.title: Try It
note.paragraph: Rewrite as equivalent rational expressions with denominator $$(x + 3)(x - 4)(x + 4)$$ : $$\frac{2}{x^{2} - x - 12},\frac{1}{x^{2} - 16}.$$

note.title: Try It
note.paragraph: Rewrite as equivalent rational expressions with denominator $$(x + 3)(x + 5)(x + 6)$$ : $$\frac{x}{x^{2} + 8x + 15},\frac{5}{x^{2} + 9x + 18}.$$

section.heading: Add Rational Expressions with Different Denominators
section.paragraph: Now we have all the steps we need to add rational expressions with different denominators. As we have done previously, we will do one example of adding numerical fractions first.

row.cell: Rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction with the LCD.

section.paragraph: Now we will add rational expressions whose denominators are monomials.

row.cell: Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent fraction with the LCD.
There are no factors common to the numerator and denominator. The fraction cannot be simplified.

section.paragraph: Now we are ready to tackle polynomial denominators.

example.title: How to Add Rational Expressions with Different Denominators

section.paragraph: The steps to use to add rational expressions are summarized in the following procedure box.

list.item: Step 1. Determine if the expressions have a common denominator. Yes – go to step 2. No – Rewrite each rational expression with the LCD. Find the LCD. Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.

row.cell: Do the expressions have a common denominator? No. Rewrite each expression with the LCD.
Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.
There are no factors common to the numerator and denominator. The fraction cannot be simplified.

section.paragraph: Avoid the temptation to simplify too soon! In the example above, we must leave the first rational expression as $$\frac{2a\left( {2a - b} \right)}{b\left( {2a + b} \right)\left( {2a - b} \right)}$$ to be able to add it to $$\frac{3a \cdot b}{\left( {2a + b} \right)\left( {2a - b} \right) \cdot b}$$ . Simplify only after you have combined the numerators.

row.cell: Do the expressions have a common denominator? No. Rewrite each expression with the LCD.
Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent fraction with the LCD.
The numerator is prime, so there are no common factors.

section.heading: Subtract Rational Expressions with Different Denominators
section.paragraph: The process we use to subtract rational expressions with different denominators is the same as for addition. We just have to be very careful of the signs when subtracting the numerators.

example.title: How to Subtract Rational Expressions with Different Denominators

section.paragraph: The steps to take to subtract rational expressions are listed below.

list.item: Step 1. Determine if they have a common denominator. Yes – go to step 2. No – Rewrite each rational expression with the LCD. Find the LCD. Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.

row.cell: Do the expressions have a common denominator? No. Rewrite each expression with the LCD.
Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.
Factor the numerator to look for common factors.

section.paragraph: There are lots of negative signs in the next example. Be extra careful!

row.cell: Since $$n - 2$$ and $$2 - n$$ are opposites, we will mutliply the second rational expression by $$\frac{-1}{-1}$$ .
Do the expressions have a common denominator? No.
Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.
Factor the numerator to look for common factors.

section.paragraph: When one expression is not in fraction form, we can write it as a fraction with denominator 1.

row.cell: Write $$3$$ as $$\frac{3}{1}$$ to have 2 rational expressions.
Do the rational expressions have a common denominator? No.
Find the LCD of $$c - 2$$ and $$1.$$ LCD = $$c - 2.$$
Rewrite $$\frac{3}{1}$$ as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.
Factor to check for common factors.
There are no common factors; the rational expression is simplified.

list.item: Step 1. Determine if the expressions have a common denominator. Yes – go to step 2. No – Rewrite each rational expression with the LCD. Find the LCD. Rewrite each rational expression as an equivalent rational expression with the LCD.
Step 2. Add or subtract the rational expressions.

section.paragraph: We follow the same steps as before to find the LCD when we have more than two rational expressions. In the next example we will start by factoring all three denominators to find their LCD.
